CHALLENGE C0011 | `compute_pacing_signals()` documents `context_budget` as "Per-model context budget from config" and `EndocrineLayer.run()` passes a single per-model scalar by default. Taking `max(dict.values())` is consistent with collapsing per-model overrides to one threshold-like budget signal; summing budgets would compare one model's cumulative context against total fleet budget and under-trigger. This is interface dishonesty/typing debt, but the proposed sum fix is wrong.
MERGE C0007 <- F001 | same root cause: `compute_pacing_signals()` accepts/handles a dict budget despite scalar API; the issue is interface inconsistency, not arithmetic choice.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` has an interface/type contract mismatch that can crash at runtime when called with non-`int` scalar numerics. The signature says `context_budget: int`, but the implementation only special-cases `dict` and then performs `if context_budget > 0:` followed by division. If a caller passes `None`, a string from config/env parsing, or any other non-int scalar-ish value, this raises `TypeError` inside endocrine between rounds. Evidence: there is no validation/coercion after the dict branch, and `EndocrineLayer.run()` forwards `context_budget` directly.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine→insect-brain pacing interface. A bad config value or override shape aborts pacing computation for the whole round report, which means the endocrine cycle can fail after health scan and fix evaluation have already run. In a PoC this is a HIGH silent integration hazard because pacing is supposed to be a mechanical monitor; instead a malformed budget value can drop the whole endocrine report path rather than degrading to “no context signal”.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — validate/coerce at function entry: after the existing dict handling, require `context_budget` to be an `int` or `float`, otherwise default to `80_000` (or return no context-growth signal). This preserves end-to-end operation without expanding the API surface.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox test execution against the patched codebase. It writes only the patched target file into a temp dir, then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir` unchanged. Any test command that references the real repository by path or imports modules from the original checkout will execute against unpatched source, while only linters/type-checkers inspect `patched_path`. Evidence: the sandbox contains just `os.path.basename(target_path)`, not the repo tree or package layout; `test_cmd` is passed through verbatim; nothing rewrites paths, `PYTHONPATH`, or module roots to point imports at the temp copy. The module docstring claims “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)” and the capability description says fix evaluation answers “does the proposed fix break anything?”, but tests are not bound to the patched artifact.
FOLLOW: This directly affects the key endocrine capability used by the immune pipeline’s Stage 4. A fix can be marked SAFE because tests passed against original code, or marked HARMFUL/NEUTRAL based only on static-tool deltas while the runtime behavior of the patch was never exercised. Downstream, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` sets `finding.verified = True` for SAFE/NEUTRAL results, which activates the bug-closed gate and suppresses future reports. That creates silently wrong closure of unresolved bugs — a HIGH PoC failure because reviewer-facing verification output becomes misleading.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, copy the full source tree needed for imports into the tempdir and patch the target file at its relative path there, then run tests against that temp tree with `cwd=tmpdir`. If relative-tree copying is unavailable from current inputs, skip runtime tests and leave `tests_passed=None` rather than pretending the existing command tested the patch.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can overwrite the wrong file inside the sandbox when multiple source files share the same basename. It writes the patched file to `tmpdir / os.path.basename(target_path)` and runs tool checks on that flattened path. Evidence: directory structure is discarded entirely. If `source_paths` contains e.g. `bench/endocrine.py` and another `foo/endocrine.py`, both map to the same sandbox filename. The target resolver `_find_target_file()` already allows loose substring matches, so basename collisions are plausible in multi-module repos.
FOLLOW: This breaks both correctness and the “never modifies actual source”/sandbox isolation story. Static tools may analyze the wrong file contents under the wrong path, and test execution cannot preserve package/module identity. Downstream verdicts SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL then refer to a corrupted sandbox artifact, which can verify or reject fixes for the wrong module. In the immune pipeline that can wrongly mark unrelated findings verified and close them out.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — preserve the target file’s relative path inside the tempdir instead of flattening to basename; create parent directories as needed before writing the patched file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses aggregate net issue count across pyright/ruff/bandit, so a fix that introduces new errors in one dimension can still be labeled SAFE if it removes more issues elsewhere. Evidence: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; only `total_net > 0` is harmful, `total_net < 0` is safe. Example: `+2` new pyright errors and `-3` ruff issues yields `total_net = -1` => SAFE despite regressions. This contradicts the docstring “SAFE: no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: This contaminates the core verification signal exposed to the immune pipeline. A patch that breaks type safety or introduces a new security warning can still be treated as SAFE, leading Stage 4 in `immune_agents.py` to set `verified=True` and close the bug. Because this is silent and reviewer-facing, it is HIGH severity in PoC terms.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; only classify as SAFE when all individual nets are `<= 0` and at least one is negative or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.81
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the tool inventory and stated capabilities are internally inconsistent in a way that leaves advertised health-scan features dead. `CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `PYTHON_313`, and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are defined; the module header advertises mypy and crosshair binaries; but no crosshair runner exists and `scan_health()` never invokes crosshair. This is distinct from generic category dead code: an entire listed analyzer is unreachable.
FOLLOW: Downstream health reports systematically omit one of the declared analyzers while still presenting as a full “whole-body health monitor”. That misleads reviewers about coverage and can skew pacing/health decisions if they assume symbolic execution is contributing. For PoC this is MEDIUM but quick to fix because it is pure interface honesty.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove crosshair from the documented/tool constant surface for now (and delete unused constants), or add it to `scan_health()` with a minimal runner. The simpler PoC correction is to remove the dead advertised support.
VERIFIED: TRUE
